Rerun a job.

## Synopsis

```text
rerun [jobid=<jobid>[,...]] [since_jobid=<since_jobid>]
      [until_jobid=<until_jobid>] [days=<days>] [hours=<hours>] [yes]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Starts earlier jobs again with the parameters they ran with (job, level, client, fileset, pool). Jobs are chosen by JobId, by a JobId range with since\_jobid= and until\_jobid=, or by a time window with days= and hours=. For every job the Director shows the run summary and asks yes, mod or no; yes on the command line starts all chosen jobs without asking.

since\_jobid=, days= and hours= consider only jobs that ended with a fatal error (status f); for days= and hours= the scheduled start time counts, and both values add up. until\_jobid= is only valid together with since\_jobid=. Before rerunning several jobs found this way the Director lists the JobIds and asks for confirmation.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobid=` | string |  |  | list | Job ID. |
| `since_jobid=` | integer |  |  |  | Rerun failed jobs since this JobId. |
| `until_jobid=` | integer |  |  |  | Up to this JobId. |
| `days=` | integer |  |  |  | Failed jobs of the last days. |
| `hours=` | integer |  |  |  | Failed jobs of the last hours. |
| `yes` | keyword |  |  |  | Do not ask. |

## Examples

Run job 42 again with its original parameters:

```text
rerun jobid=42
```

Restart every job that failed during the last day:

```text
rerun days=1 yes
```

Failed jobs between JobId 100 and 120:

```text
rerun since_jobid=100 until_jobid=120
```
